messages:

Sam

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on metering for our POC

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions, and great to see the usage file. Short answer up front: Responses and Chat are billed on the same hosted token primitives, but there are a couple of important differences that affect unit math and how it appears in reporting.

Key points:
- Metering primitive: we bill on token-in + token-out for hosted text generation. Responses uses the same token primitives as Chat, so unit costs per token are the same for the same model family and precision.
- Endpoint differences: legacy /v1/chat/completions calls are still supported; they map to the same token buckets but on invoices will show the legacy endpoint label if you used it. Responses calls appear with the Responses label. Both roll up to the same model SKU in the final usage CSV.
- Practical discrepancy: Responses currently includes additional structured metadata overhead (tool calls, function args) which can increase counted tokens slightly on some workloads — we typically see ~2-4% delta in token accounting vs equivalent raw Chat input because of wrapper tokens and tooling traces.

I’m looping in Aditya to confirm how that delta shows up in the invoice rows and whether we can provide an aggregated sample export for your POC.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

3) Commit/discounts: for a $120k/12mo ARR commitment we can offer the following baseline pricing pathway (hosted API):

   - Committed effective: $0.0011 per token after the 12-month commit (applies to billed tokens net of refunds/chargebacks)
   - Additional: tiered volume rebates at 250M+ tokens/month; professional services credits for onboarding included at the $120k commit level

4) Next steps: Jasmine will send the sanitized invoice + an exported usage CSV and a worked example that maps your 120M tokens/mo to monthly spend (with the 3% overhead baked in). If that aligns, I’ll get legal to prepare the commitment language and the finance team will provide the purchase sequence.

Would you like us to model both optimistic (no overhead) and conservative (+3%) scenarios in the worked example?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
